positive_styles: cinematic anime opening rock anthem
F-sharp minor
80 BPM melody over 160 BPM double-time drums
solo female lead vocal, alto to mezzo, strong chest voice, slightly raspy grainy edge, direct and unpolished, minimal vibrato, clear English diction
a cappella for this section, close and dry
the first note is short and low, the second leaps a full octave up and is held
defiant, hopeful, urgent
instrumental
huge full-band hit on beat one
live drum kit at 160 BPM, tight and punchy
foot stamps on wooden planks and hand claps on the backbeat
harp and string pizzicato ostinato in eighth notes grouped 3+3+2
punchy bass guitar in short notes
one sharp two-finger whistle at the end
group shout 'Hey!' in unison

chunks.text:
[Verse]
Down where the lanterns float in the street,
we keep the time with our hands and our feet.
Up on the towers the song is for sale —
calm can be bought by the ones who don't bail.
Whistle the warning, the water is high:
so who's gonna pay for the dry?
positive_styles: female lead vocal in the middle register, rhythmic and tight
each line starts with a short note and leaps up to the stressed word
drums at half intensity: rimshots, claps, kick
string ostinato continues
bass guitar short notes
building tension
street energy, stubborn

chunks.text:
[Pre-Chorus]
Keep your head down, keep it in your chest,
let the ones up high do the rest —
but the water's at the window,
and the hollow stone won't save us now...
{full stop, half a beat of silence before the chorus}
positive_styles: melody climbs to a high F-sharp and settles on a long held C-sharp
French horns answer the voice with proud descending calls
harmony climbs D major, E major, C-sharp suspended, C-sharp major
snare drum roll building
rising tension
ends with a sudden silent gap

chunks.text:
[Chorus]
Sing — louder than the tide,
we were never made to hide.
Sing — louder than the tide:
this voice is all we own.
positive_styles: anthemic chorus, full power
the melody leaps a full octave on 'louder' right after the downbeat
female lead vocal belting in chest voice
live drums at 160 BPM full energy, big crash on the downbeat
overdriven rhythm guitar wall
strings and French horns in unison with the vocal melody
foot stamps and hand claps on the backbeat
catchy, easy to sing along

chunks.text:
[Bridge]
They can buy the calm and the quiet,
and the water keeps its counsel —
{band drops out, only stamps and claps}
(Who's gonna pay?)
positive_styles: sudden drop to near silence
intimate low female voice, almost spoken, with one solo cello
then only foot stamps and hand claps
group shout in unison, not sung
snare fill into the final chorus

chunks.text:
[Final Chorus]
Sing — louder than the tide:
this voice is all we own!
positive_styles: biggest moment of the song
octave leap on 'louder' right after the downbeat
the last word held long on the high fifth, open and unresolved
full band, strings and horns in unison with the voice
stamps and claps at full
triumphant and desperate at once

chunks.text:
[Outro]
{one final full-band hit, ringing open fifth, clean decay}
positive_styles: instrumental
single final hit on an open fifth F-sharp and C-sharp, no third
harp and cymbal tail
clean natural decay to silence
